pageCache.pageTitle: Monken Hadley Primary School - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Collective Worship is an important part of our school day and helps us grow as a thoughtful, caring and fully inclusive community. Each day, we come together for Collective Worship, gathering as a whole school to pause, reflect and think about the values that shape how we live and learn together. This daily rhythm gives children a sense of belonging, purpose and calm.
Our worship is welcoming and inclusive of all pupils, staff and families. Every child is invited to take part in ways that feel right for them through singing, quiet reflection, prayer, reading, drama, discussion or offering their own thoughts. These moments of stillness and celebration help children develop confidence, empathy and a growing awareness of themselves and others.
We explore themes such as kindness, respect, forgiveness, courage and service, drawing on stories, traditions and ideas from Christianity as well as other world religions. British Values — democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance — are woven naturally into our worship themes. Children learn how these values help us to treat one another fairly, listen to different viewpoints and contribute positively to our community.
Our worship also reflects and respects the protected characteristics. We celebrate diversity, promote equality and ensure that every child feels seen, valued and included. Worship often includes opportunities to explore identity, belonging and difference in age‑appropriate ways, helping children understand and appreciate the richness of our school community.
We enjoy a close relationship with St Mary’s Church. The Rector leads a weekly whole‑school service, and we visit the church regularly to mark special times in the year. We also welcome visitors from local churches and the theological college who enrich our worship with different perspectives and experiences.
Alongside whole‑school worship, children take part in our Let's Be Still and daily prayers, giving them regular opportunities to pause, reflect and connect their learning with their own developing sense of spirituality.
Through this varied pattern of worship, children are encouraged to think deeply, respond creatively and grow in confidence, compassion and understanding.
Collective Worship Policy

Attendance
Monken Hadley operates a soft start in the morning. This means children can start coming into class from 8.35am. The gates close at 8.45am when the register is taken. It is really important that your child is in school in time for registration at 8.45 am. Children who arrive from 8.35 will complete early morning work set by the teacher. Being punctual for school is not only a life skill, but the mornings are a key time where the teachers explain the day ahead and share any key information.
School finishes at 3:15pm
Total Time in School
The total time in school in a typical week is 32.5 hours
If your child is absent please call the school office before 8:50am and notify them. If your child is ill the office will ask for more information with regards to the symptoms of your child's illness.
Please note the school will not authorise absence for holidays.
More information regarding attendance can be found in our parent handbook.

St Mary's Church
For our 188 years we have been in partnership with St Mary's Church. Our school badge is a direct replica of the famous beacon that sits on top of the church, the highest point for many miles.
The church rector is Francesco Aresco. Francesco also serves on the school's Governing Body.
Local Diocese
Monken Hadley is part of two diocese. Locally we fall into Edmonton Diocese which is led by Bishop Anderson and more broadly into the London Diocese led by Bishop Sarah Mullally.

pageCache.pageTitle: Monken Hadley Primary School - Inspection Reports
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
Monken Hadley is inspected by two bodies: OFSTED and SIAMS.
The aim of the SIAMS inspection, commissioned by the Department of Education for all church schools, is to look at how effective the school's distinctive Christian vision is, how it is established and promoted by leadership at all levels and the effectiveness of the teaching of RE.
In February 2023 the school received both Ofsted and SIAMS inspections.
We are delighted that both inspections went well and the school received a judgement of Outstanding in all areas from Ofsted and Excellent in all areas from SIAMS.
There are many positive comments in each of the reports; here are some of our highlights:
We are so incredibly proud of our school, the children, staff, governors and wider parent community. This is a huge recognition of the school and the journey we are on.

The Governing Body School Governors are the school’s Board of Directors. The purpose of the Governing Body is:
to help the school set high standards by planning for the school's future, and setting targets for school improvements.
to be a critical friend to the school, offering the school its support and advice.
to help the school to be responsive to the needs of parents and the community and to make the school more accountable to the public for what it does.
Working together, Governors make decisions about the running of the school. The whole Governing Body meets nine times a year (approximately once each month).
We endeavour for the GB to reflect the school in terms of the school's diversity. If would like more information regarding this please contact the school office.

Parents
Welcome to Monken Hadley and our community. You are all a key part of our school and it is certainly true that great parents help to make great schools.
We have an open door policy at school and if you need to speak to your child's teacher please catch them at the end of the school day. Alternatively you can contact them via the Class email or the Office e-mail.
A weekly newsletter is e-mailed on Fridays with news about forthcoming events and most importantly what learning has been taking place in each that week across our Curiosity Curriculum.
Parent involvement in the school is welcomed and if you have a skill you would like to share or some time you would like to give please do let us know.
As a learning community, we are always looking at ways to grow and develop so everyone here at school can flourish.

London Diocesan Board of Schools
The Church of England has been establishing and sustaining schools for the people of London for hundreds of years. In 1836 the London Diocesan Board for Schools was established to support the rapid increase in the number of new schools in the Diocese of London. In 1924 the Board was incorporated as a charitable company.
Key purposes of the LDBS are “to promote church schools” and “to promote education which is consistent with the faith and practice of the Church of England”.
To achieve these purposes, the LDBS support over 160 Church of England Schools, 2 community schools and a community nursery in a variety of ways across 18 North London local authorities.
